title: CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619: Critical Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution in PHP
summary: On October 21, 2026, the PHP project announced security releases for two critical vulnerabilities in PHP. CVE-2026-109618 can corrupt memory during out-of-memory (OOM) handling, while CVE-2026-109619 is a use-after-free flaw involving state retained between requests. Both have a CVSSv4 score of 9.2 and both can allow for unauthenticated remote code execution (RCE) with the web worker's privileges.
body_markdown:
## Overview


On October 21, 2026, the PHP project


[announced security releases](https://www.php.net/archive/2026.php#2026-10-21-5) for two critical vulnerabilities in PHP.


[CVE-2026-109618](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-109618) can corrupt memory during out-of-memory (OOM) handling, while


[CVE-2026-109619](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-109619) is a use-after-free flaw involving state retained between requests. Both have a CVSSv4 score of 9.2 and both can allow for unauthenticated remote code execution (RCE) with the web worker's privileges.


**CVE**


**CVSSv4**


**Description**


[CVE-2026-109618](https://github.com/php/php-src/security/advisories/GHSA-w8hw-w9fx-j79w)


[9.2 (Critical)](https://www.first.org/cvss/calculator/4.0#CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:H/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N)


RCE via OOM corruption


[CVE-2026-109619](https://github.com/php/php-src/security/advisories/GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp)


RCE via stale global state


All installations serving web requests are at risk, including PHP-FPM, Apache mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP, and LiteSpeed. The vendor considers mod_php the highest risk because exploitation can succeed before any application code runs.


The advisories report that a successful RCE exploit was developed during research, including achieving RCE against Apache mod_php and PHP-FPM through different attack paths. As of October 21, 2026, there are multiple indications that this research is being independently reproduced, and a viable exploit is expected to be made public soon.


Due to the extremely high deployment of PHP based web applications, exploitation in-the-wild is expected.


**Rapid7 recommends updating affected installations on an emergency basis, outside of normal patch cycles.**


Multiple public proof-of-concept (PoC) exploits for CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 are now available. Rapid7 researchers have reviewed these and observe that each demonstrates RCE only against a specific combination of operating system, PHP version, and web server, and none appears to be broadly reliable. Rapid7’s own research supports this. Our attempts so far have produced a working exploit only under narrow lab conditions, and exploitation depends on assumptions that are unlikely to hold on internet-facing instances. We are continuing to investigate approaches that could improve portability, but have not yet developed a reliable, general-purpose exploit. Rapid7 has not observed exploitation in the wild, though there are multiple reports of exploitation attempts, which is expected for a vulnerability of this profile. The situation is evolving quickly, and a more portable exploit technique could emerge at any time. The current difficulty of reliable exploitation should be treated as a window to patch rather than a reason to delay, and Rapid7 continues to recommend updating affected installations on an emergency basis.


**Update #1**


: On October 26, 2026,


[CVE-2026-109618](https://www.rapid7.com/db/vulnerabilities/cve-2026-109618/) and


[CVE-2026-109619](https://www.rapid7.com/db/vulnerabilities/cve-2026-109619/) were


[added to the U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency's (CISA) list of known exploited vulnerabilities (KEV)](https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog) , based on evidence of active exploitation. CISA set the remediation due date to October 29, 2026, for affected Federal Civilian Executive Branch agencies and directs them to follow the associated


[BOD 26-04 forensic triage requirements](https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/directives/bod-26-04-implementation-guidance-prioritizing-security-updates-based-risk) . Rapid7 continues to recommend updating affected installations on an emergency basis and investigating for prior compromise.


## Technical overview


### CVE-2026-109618: Memory corruption during OOM handling


According to the


[OOM advisory](https://github.com/php/php-src/security/advisories/GHSA-w8hw-w9fx-j79w) , PHP can abruptly abandon request processing when a memory allocation fails. If internal request data is only partly initialized, that exit can leave invalid data for request cleanup to use. Crafted multipart requests, used for forms and file uploads, can exhaust memory even when their size appears to meet PHP's configured limits. Application operations that allocate memory in response to attacker input can also trigger OOM.


Apache mod_php runs cleanup even when request startup fails, enabling the demonstrated attack before application code executes. The advisory reports RCE over HTTP with default PHP input and memory limits, including multi-worker prefork deployments. PHP-FPM terminates a worker when startup fails, preventing that particular sequence. Source analysis supports FPM susceptibility after successful startup, but the advisory reports no complete FPM exploit for this CVE. Exploit portability and reliability depend on the PHP build, extensions, frontend behavior, and memory layout.


### CVE-2026-109619: Use after free across requests


PHP can reuse a worker process to handle multiple HTTP requests. The


[stale-state advisory](https://github.com/php/php-src/security/advisories/GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp) describes internal state that still points to memory freed at the end of an earlier request. A later request handled by the same worker can access that stale value before normal initialization clears it. Fatal errors, including memory exhaustion and execution timeouts, can interrupt state cleanup; some nonfatal diagnostics during shutdown can also repopulate error state after it was reset.


The advisory confirms RCE against mod_php through PHP 8.5's fatal error backtrace feature, when


fatal_error_backtraces


is enabled (the default), where a later initialization diagnostic accesses stale backtrace state. It also confirms session lifecycle RCE against mod_php and FPM. Session upload progress, PHP's upload-tracking feature, is enabled by default and can act as an early consumer of stale session or decoder state before normal initialization; reaching this consumer does not itself require an application call to


session_start()


.


The validated FPM session path requires a suitable application operation to leave state behind after successful startup, followed by a fatal error and another request that consumes the stale state through session upload progress. Both requests must reach the same worker. Multiple workers and worker recycling can reduce success per request, but do not eliminate the condition.


## Mitigation guidance


PHP has released fixes for both vulnerabilities. Organizations should prioritize updating to the appropriate fixed release or a vendor package containing both complete patches. The PHP advisories list these affected and fixed versions:


-


PHP 8.2 releases before 8.2.35: Update to 8.2.35


-


PHP 8.3 releases before 8.3.36: Update to 8.3.36


-


PHP 8.4 releases before 8.4.27: Update to 8.4.27


-


PHP 8.5 releases before 8.5.12: Update to 8.5.12


Linux distributions and long-term support vendors received patches in advance; check your vendor for updated packages. PHP 8.1 and older no longer receive routine upstream updates. For this incident, PHP has supplied limited source backports for


[PHP 7.4](https://github.com/php/php-src/tree/PHP-7.4-CVE-2026-109618-109619) ,


[8.0](https://github.com/php/php-src/tree/PHP-8.0-CVE-2026-109618-109619) , and


[8.1](https://github.com/php/php-src/tree/PHP-8.1-CVE-2026-109618-109619) . Organizations running older branches should obtain a vendor fix, use the source backports described in the


[PHP announcement](https://www.php.net/archive/2026.php#2026-10-21-5) , or upgrade to a supported version. PHP also warns that


rpms.remirepo.net


will not have updates on October 21, 2026, and urges its users to switch to distribution packages or build from source.


**Note that an update containing both complete fixes is the only complete remediation.**


PHP's temporary configuration measures


*reduce*


exposure to specific paths and require careful deployment:


-


For the OOM issue, enforce


memory_limit=-1


administratively, such as through FPM pool or Apache configuration that applications cannot override. This disables PHP's per-request memory cap and removes the predictable PHP-limit failure used by the confirmed exploit. An underlying allocation failure can still reach the vulnerable path. Restart every worker and verify that no pool, directory, or application setting restores a finite limit.


-


For the session lifecycle path, set


session.upload_progress.enabled=0


in


php.ini


, an FPM pool, or server configuration that applies before request parsing, then restart every worker. Application-level


ini_set()


and FPM


.user.ini


are too late. This addresses the confirmed session paths only.


-


On PHP 8.5, set


fatal_error_backtraces=0


administratively and restart every worker. This addresses the confirmed fatal backtrace path only; other retained state remains a concern.


Disabling PHP's memory cap makes independent resource controls particularly important. PHP recommends


post_max_size=8M


where uploads are unnecessary or


post_max_size=32M


where they are needed, with


upload_max_filesize


below that limit. At the frontend, bound decoded request size, input and multipart counts, headers per part, and nesting depth, including requests without a usable


Content-Length


. If the application does not use multipart data, block those requests before they reach PHP.


Container or cgroup memory limits are also incomplete: allocation failures remain possible, and enforcement can kill the master process and all workers unless workers are isolated. Do not substitute


RLIMIT_AS


or


RLIMIT_DATA


, which can trigger the vulnerable allocation-failure path.


For stale-state exposure, correct invalid or deprecated per-request settings and attacker-reachable fatal errors or timeouts. Hiding diagnostics through


error_reporting


,


display_errors


,


log_errors


, or


@


does not prevent stale-state access. The absence of relevant log entries is not proof that an installation is safe.


For the latest mitigation guidance, refer to PHP's


[OOM corruption advisory](https://github.com/php/php-src/security/advisories/GHSA-w8hw-w9fx-j79w) and


[stale global state advisory](https://github.com/php/php-src/security/advisories/GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp) .


## Rapid7 customers


To learn how to use Rapid7 capabilities to find systems affected by these vulnerabilities and for answers to common questions, read the


[PHP2Shell documentation](https://docs.rapid7.com/insightvm/php2shell/) .


For Rapid7 Customers with questions regarding Rapid7 products and their usage of PHP please consult[this page.](https://www.rapid7.com/trust/advisories/php-cve-2026-109618-cve-2026-109619/)


### Exposure Command, Vulnerability Management, and Nexpose


Exposure Command, Vulnerability Management, and Nexpose customers can assess exposure to CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 with remote unauthenticated vulnerability checks, available in a dedicated release that followed the regular October 21 content release.


Rapid7 has also released authenticated scan checks for both the Scan Engine and the Agent for CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 as part of the October 22 content release.


Authenticated, package-based checks are now available for a variety of Linux distributions. These checks evaluate installed distribution packages, so they can recognize backported fixes that keep the original upstream PHP version number. Run an authenticated scan with this content release to use them. For the full list of checks and supported distribution versions, read Rapid7’s


[PHP2Shell documentation](https://docs.rapid7.com/insightvm/php2shell/#31-exposure-command-vulnerability-management-insightvm-and-nexpose) , where package-based coverage for other distributions will be added as their fixes are published.


In a dedicated October 23 content release following the regular release, Rapid7 has released coverage for CVE-2026-115560,


[published on October 23](https://www.php.net/archive/2026.php#2026-10-23-1) by the PHP Foundation. A mitigation technique is available, but no patch has yet been published. Exploitation of CVE-2026-115560 relies on non-standard configuration.


*Current*


*scope for authenticated coverage: Windows, macOS and Linux. Remote unauthenticated coverage provides coverage regardless of web-server OS.*


### Velociraptor


A Velociraptor Artifact


[Generic.Applications.PHPInventory](https://docs.velociraptor.app/exchange/artifacts/pages/phpinventory/) is available to inventory PHP installations on Windows, Linux and macOS for remediation scoping. This artifact allows for the collection of package versions, common binary and module paths, and running PHP processes.
